title: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)
hook: Arjuna is given a divine eye to see Krishna's universal form, and among the faces rushing into it are names the blind king knows.
tomorrow: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Bhishma Parva, Arjuna argued: you were born after the sun. And Krishna answered: I know my births, and you don't; better your own duty, done imperfectly, than someone else's done well. Did you do a task without checking how it landed? Day eight hundred twenty-three.

Two people in this story are given eyes they weren't born with. One is Sanjaya, who sees the whole battlefield from the palace so he can tell the king. Another is Arjuna, who in the eleventh chapter of the Gita asks to see Krishna as he truly is, and is told his ordinary eyes can't do it. So Krishna gives him a divine eye. And then there's us, listening, because the one describing Arjuna's vision is Sanjaya, speaking to a blind father. Session five of six: the vision, heard from inside the palace.
screen: `EYES THEY WEREN'T BORN WITH` → `ARJUNA GETS A DIVINE EYE` → `SANJAYA TELLS THE BLIND KING`

segments.voice: Arjuna sees a form with countless faces and eyes, a light like a thousand suns rising at once, the whole universe gathered in one body. In the Gita it's Sanjaya who says this to Dhritarashtra. Then the vision turns. Arjuna sees the warriors of the war rushing into terrible mouths, like rivers racing to the sea, like moths into a flame. And he names them. The sons of Dhritarashtra. Bhishma. Drona. Karna. Our own warriors too. Now hear it from where the king sits. He refused to watch this war. He asked only to be told. And here, in the middle of a teaching about God, Sanjaya tells him his own sons are among the faces disappearing into those mouths. Arjuna, shaking, asks: who are you? And Krishna answers: I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of worlds. Even without you, none of these warriors will survive. They are already slain by me. Be only the instrument. Then he names them again: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna. Read alone, this chapter is a vision of the divine. Read in place, it's also a forecast, spoken over the heads of real men who are standing in their ranks, waiting. Bhishma is one of them. The book named for him has already told us he will fall. And at the end, Arjuna, terrified, asks to see his friend's familiar face again. Krishna takes his gentle form, and Arjuna says: now I'm myself again.
screen: `A THOUSAND SUNS AT ONCE` · `THE WARRIORS RUSH INTO THE MOUTHS` · `I AM TIME. BE THE INSTRUMENT.` · then, large: `THE FAMILIAR FACE AGAIN`

segments.voice: Sit and let your gaze go soft. For a breath or two, widen your attention: the room, the building, the street, the sky over it. Let it be big. Then, gently, come back. Back to the room. Back to your hands. Back to one familiar thing near you: a cup, a chair, your own breath. Stay there. Arjuna saw everything, and then asked for the familiar face. Both are allowed. If you pray, you can rest your prayer on that familiar thing. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma Parva. The book whose grandsire stands in the ranks while Arjuna's vision names him among those Time has already taken.
Your line: now I'm myself again. Today, after something big, come back to one familiar face and stay with it a while. Day eight hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: The vision of the universal form in the Gita's eleventh chapter is read and recited, and it appears in temple art and paintings showing Krishna with many faces and arms before Arjuna's chariot.

match.prompt: who saw what? tap the pairs.
pairs: sees the battle to tell the king
given a divine eye by Krishna
hears his sons named in the vision
I am Time, destroyer of worlds

myth: Arjuna could see the universal form with his ordinary eyes
Krishna says he can't, and gives him a divine eye.
Bhishma, Drona and Karna are named in Arjuna's vision
he sees them rushing into the mouths, and Krishna names them too.
Arjuna asked to keep seeing the vision forever
terrified, he asked to see Krishna's familiar form again.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. you've seen the universe in your friend's body, and warriors you know rushing into its mouths. you're shaking. what do you ask?
options: let me see your familiar form again.
tell me how to stop this war.
fork.reveal: he asks to see Krishna's gentle form again. Krishna takes it, and Arjuna says he is himself once more.

original.note: kala, time: what Krishna names himself in the vision, the destroyer of worlds.

trapdoor: what you thought: the universal form is a vision of the divine and nothing else.
what it means: in place, it also names who will die: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, the king's own sons.
what a scholar hears: Sanjaya's report means the blind father hears his sons' fate inside a vision of God.

notes: All paraphrase.
